brief.title: Midterm brief: Saturday, October 31
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Saturday, October 31

## Bottom line
Forecasters rate the House as leaning Democratic; all 10 House forecasters have more seats rated for Democrats, and Cook now has 222 D / 195 R with 18 tossups, up from 220 / 198 / 17 ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Senate is closer: 47 D and 44 R seats are solid or likely, with 9 competitive ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Markets price Democratic control at 94.5% for the House and 70.5% for the Senate, the Senate up two points ([Polymarket House](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026), [Senate](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026)), as of Oct 31.

## What moved
- **Forecaster updates (Oct 29-30):** 74 rating changes, 42 toward Democrats and 32 toward Republicans ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). Cook made 14 and Decision Desk HQ 9, all toward Democrats; The Economist made 18, all toward Republicans; Silver Bulletin made 22 in both directions.
- **House consensus:** NY-17 moved from Tossup to Lean D; PA-08 from Tilt D to Lean D; WI-01 from Tossup to Lean R.
- **Polls:** Kansas Senate's average moved from D+1.5 to D+3.6 across 4 polls; MT-01's from D+2.2 to D+8.0 across 3.
- **Senate ratings:** Silver Bulletin moved Alaska from Lean D to Tossup and Kansas from Tossup to Lean D; Cook moved Nebraska to Lean R ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). No tracked Senate consensus changed.

## Races to watch today
- **Kansas Senate (Tossup):** An Emerson poll finds Hamilton keeping an edge over Marshall ([Emerson Polling via Google News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMingFBVV95cUxOTlBINU11RVpHR29ySHJlQkIzRkREalllTkFJUnprQTlnYTVhanZwUXVuNGpKY3djRi0xbmFBRmpIVklSTTdyblgtMDF4bU9WSDl4YWJ2Z25NbmtyT1gwWGhfR3F6dGV1Q1cwMkhVTF9Na1BoeGlLdU9KbUJ6XzF3b0ZkTFJFelpZb0hCUHg0ampTcWdYV09GWkVkN2NGUQ?oc=5)), and Trump will now rally for Marshall on Sunday ([KCUR via Google News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMixAFBVV95cUxQYWRNemxoVjdXY0FDWHRMdkF2Y3F5d0NMc2dNWFN4aGxjSEdZeV92aWhHeVlRdFcyT0R1R3o4bm5FYnoyNUJCdkRrM2NqTXZUSUt3WkRVWlI3dnFvbFRZNEtpYjNVNE5FRWRoaHlOQjBkd09Iclp6T0xldW5MN0x2eE9OY1JfR0Vkdm9EbG8zUWtxVzVaWW1ZVS1tdVAtU3FmM3hKWkVPMjR3SWh6SHhOazZoaGxBbmMzeUE1SVJiU25YSjB2?oc=5)). Average: D+3.6.
- **Nebraska Senate (Lean R):** A new Times/Siena poll finds Ricketts leading independent Dan Osborn ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/31/us/politics/nebraska-senate-poll.html)). It is not in the average yet (R+2.3).
- **Iowa Senate (Tossup):** The NYT reports Democrats remain jittery about Iowa despite hopes elsewhere ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/30/us/politics/iowa-senate-race-josh-turek.html)). Average: R+0.2.
- **Michigan Senate (Lean D):** El-Sayed clashed with former primary rival Haley Stevens ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/30/us/politics/el-sayed-stevens-michigan-senate-event.html)). Average: D+4.0.

## Early vote
These are ballots by party registration, not votes, and mail ballots have leaned Democratic since 2020.
- **North Carolina:** Through Oct 29, 2,353,233 ballots were cast, 134% of the 2022 total at the same point (1,753,484) ([NCSBE](https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Press/2026%20General/NC%20Absentee%20Stats%20for%202026%20General/2026-10-30%20Daily%20Absentee%20Stats%20Report%20-%202026%20General.pdf)). By Oct 30 the total reached 2,612,250 at D 38.7% / R 26.0% ([NCSBE data file](https://dl.ncsbe.gov/?prefix=ENRS/2026_11_03/)).
- **Florida (Oct 30):** 4,723,052 ballots at R 40.6% / D 38.1%, against registration of R 41.5% / D 30.1% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from Florida Division of Elections data).
- **Senate battlegrounds (Oct 30):** Arizona 1,542,342 at D 37.4% / R 38.0% (via a private compiler); Iowa 407,374 at D 47.1% / R 33.8%; Kansas 375,937 at R 43.0% / D 42.2%; Nebraska 215,424 at D 38.7% / R 44.1% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), from secretary of state data).
